text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- The ruling Socialist Party wants President Jorge Sampaio to decide on the dates of referenda on Europe and devolving more power to Portugal's regions.

- EU olive oil producers - Portugal, Spain, Greece, Italy and France - say they will block proposals to reform the way EU subsidies are awarded. They say the changes would choke off growth in an important sector for Mediterranean economies.
- A cabinet reshuffle is not expected at least until after December's local elections which should provide a mid-term gauge of the Socialist government's popularity, the paper said.
- The Portuguese government will provide finanicial incentives to increase the birth rate by giving more subsidies to families with three or more children, regardless of income.

- The Secretary of State for Euroepan Affairs, Seixas da Costa, says Portugal would only accept a system of rotating EU commissioners if all member states' commissioners had equal status and none had permanent positions.
- President Jorge Sampaio tells the Mozambican parliament that democracy is an ongoing process that does not end with elections.

- An audit by KPMG-Peat Marwick has found that independent television channel TVI's actual loss for 1996 was 10.41 billion escudos, nearly twice the figure the company presented in its annual report, the paper reported.
- Drought threatens winter cereal crops in the southern Alentejo region, according to the National Statistics Institute (INE).
- Portuguese investment in Mozambique will amount to more than 17 billion escudos over the next three years, Economy Minister Augusto Mateus said.
